title: Antisense oligonucleotide silencing rescues neurodevelopmental deficits in AMPA receptor gain-of-function mice
title_zh: 反义寡核苷酸沉默拯救AMPA受体功能获得小鼠的神经发育缺陷
abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission and are essential for neuronal development and brain function. We investigated the role of a recurrent AMPAR GluA1 variant (GRIA1 p.A636T) identified in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID). Using a Gria1-A636T knock-in mouse model, we show that this variant is sufficient to produce core ASD/ID-like behaviors and cause selective hippocampal vulnerability characterized by progressive dendritic atrophy and neuronal loss. Despite a reduction in GluA1-containing complexes, synaptic AMPARs exhibit hyperexcitability and fail to transition from calcium-permeable to calcium-impermeable AMPARs during development, resulting in persistent excitotoxicity. To explore potential therapeutic interventions, we developed an allele-specific antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) to selectively silence the mutant transcript. A single neonatal ASO dose prevents hippocampal pathology and rescues behavioral deficits. These findings define a mechanism of developmental excitotoxicity driven by a GRIA1 gain-of-function channelopathy and support RNA-targeted precision therapy for AMPAR-related neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract_zh: AMPA受体（AMPAR）介导快速兴奋性突触传递，对于神经元发育和脑功能至关重要。我们研究了在自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）和智力障碍（ID）患者中发现的反复出现的AMPAR GluA1变异（GRIA1 p.A636T）的作用。使用Gria1-A636T敲入小鼠模型，我们发现该变异足以产生核心ASD/ID样行为，并引起选择性海马易感性，表现为进行性树突萎缩和神经元丢失。尽管GluA1含复合物减少，但突触AMPAR表现出高兴奋性，并在发育过程中未能从钙通透型AMPAR转变为钙不通透型AMPAR，从而导致持续性兴奋性毒性。为了探索潜在治疗干预，我们开发了一种特异沉默突变转录本的等位基因专一性反义寡核苷酸（ASO）。单次新生儿ASO给药可预防海马病理并拯救行为缺陷。这些发现阐明了由GRIA1功能获得型通道病驱动的发育性兴奋性毒性机制，并为AMPAR相关神经发育障碍的RNA靶向精准治疗提供了依据。
